note: Historical event template data. Sources resolve against scenario sources[].

events.title: Airborne landings
events.body: The US 82nd and 101st Airborne on the Cotentin and the British 6th Airborne east of the Orne drop after midnight; weather and navigation scatter the drops (M09). Time of day approximate.

events.title: D-Day: the beaches
events.body: Landings begin about 06:30 at Utah, Omaha, Gold, Juno and Sword (M01). Omaha is the costliest: 2,400 casualties and 34,000 landed by the end of the day (M04); Utah costs 197 of 21,000 (M03).

events.title: 21st Panzer counter-attacks
events.body: The 21st Panzer Division counter-attacks between Sword and Juno at 16:00 and nearly reaches the coast, then is recalled to the Caen-Bayeux area (M02).

events.title: The Hitlerjugend arrives at Caen
events.body: The 12th SS Panzer Division is committed to the defence of Caen on 7 June (M12).

events.title: Panzer Lehr committed
events.body: Panzer Lehr, the Panzer Group West reserve, is released and committed against the British and Canadians on 8 June (M12).

events.title: Carentan taken, beachheads linked
events.body: The 101st Airborne forces the causeway into Carentan on 10-11 June and the Germans withdraw on 12 June; all five beachheads are connected by 12 June (M01, M10). The 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division counter-attacks on 13 June.

events.title: Villers-Bocage
events.body: The 22nd Armoured Brigade of the 7th Armoured Division takes Villers-Bocage and threatens the rear of Panzer Lehr; the Tigers of the 101st SS Heavy Panzer Battalion arrive 12-13 June and force the British back; Panzer Lehr is pushed back to Tilly-sur-Seulles by 17 June (M02, M12, M18).

events.title: The Cotentin is cut
events.body: US forces reach the west coast of the Cotentin on 17 June, cutting off Cherbourg (M02).

events.title: The Great Storm
events.body: A four-day storm batters the Channel from 19 to 22 June. Mulberry A at Omaha is wrecked before it is securely anchored and abandoned; operations are postponed (M01, M08). Mulberry B survives.
events.effectsNote: Restates M01 (storm 19-22 June, four days) and M08 (Mulberry A abandoned after the storm).

events.title: Cherbourg falls
events.body: VII Corps captures Cherbourg on 26 June (M02); another account gives 27 June (M11). The port is not cleared of mines and obstructions until 16 July (M02). This event uses the earlier date.

events.title: Operation Epsom
events.body: VIII Corps, with the 15th (Scottish) Division and the 31st Tank Brigade, attacks west of Caen on 26 June and crosses the Odon; Operation Martlet secures its flank. Bomber support is cancelled by weather (M11). The 9th and 10th SS Panzer Divisions counter-attack.

events.title: Kluge replaces Rundstedt
events.body: Rundstedt is dismissed on 1 July and Kluge becomes OB West (M02).

events.title: Operation Charnwood
events.body: Three British and Canadian infantry divisions attack Caen at dawn on 8 July after a controversial heavy-bomber raid on the city and take it up to the Orne and Odon by the next evening (M11).

events.title: Battle of Saint-Lo
events.body: The US First Army fights the Battle of Saint-Lo from 7 to 19 July in the hedgerows (M11).

events.title: Cherbourg cleared
events.body: The port of Cherbourg is cleared of mines and obstructions on 16 July and can begin to receive shipping (M02).
events.effectsNote: Restates M02 (Cherbourg cleared of mines and obstructions on 16 July); ramp time 240 h is game-scale (G01).

events.title: Operation Goodwood
events.body: VIII Corps with three armoured divisions attacks east of Caen on 18 July after a heavy-bomber raid; Operation Atlantic (II Canadian Corps) takes the southern suburbs. The armour advances 7 miles but is stopped short of Bourguebus Ridge by 20 July (M11).

events.title: Saint-Lo falls
events.body: The Battle of Saint-Lo ends on 19 July with the town in US hands (M11).

events.title: Caen is completely captured
events.body: Caen, a D-Day objective, is completely captured on 21 July (M02).

events.title: Operation Cobra
events.body: The First US Army (VII Corps, two-division assault) begins Operation Cobra on 25 July after a concentrated bombing raid, intending to break out of the bocage; friendly-fire casualties include Lt-Gen McNair (M11).

events.title: Operation Bluecoat
events.body: VIII and XXX Corps attack from Caumont towards Vire and Mont Pincon on 30 July to exploit Cobra (M11).

events.title: Avranches reached
events.body: By 31 July XIX Corps has destroyed the last forces opposing the First Army, which emerges from the bocage and liberates Avranches (M11).
